At night I keep having these awful dreams. I’m back in the gallery, hearing that crash, seeing everyone’s faces, and I wake up with my heart pounding, sometimes shaking so hard it takes me a long time to settle down. Even during the day, if there’s a sudden loud noise—a dropped crate, a door slamming—I jump out of my skin. My chest races and my hands tremble, and it lingers; I can’t just brush it off.

I’ve really lost my drive at work. I used to love giving tours, talking about the paintings, but now I struggle to even prepare my notes. I just stare at the pieces and feel…flat, or like I can’t get started. I keep going over what happened, and I find myself blaming the renovations team, and honestly the administration too—I’m convinced if they’d listened to our safety concerns, none of this would have happened. At the same time, I feel deeply ashamed, like I failed the visitors somehow, like I should have done more.

Even simple choices—what to wear, what to make for dinner—feel strangely overwhelming. I hesitate, second-guess myself, and my husband keeps asking what’s wrong, and I don’t quite know how to explain it.
D018-D020_h001.question_a:
It started about six months ago, after the robbery at the museum. The man held a gun to my head while I was leading a school tour. Since then, my sleep has been a mess. I keep having these awful dreams where I’m back in that gallery, hearing the kids scream, feeling the gun at my neck. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and it’s hard to go back to sleep.

At work I’ve just…stopped caring like I used to. I used to love planning tours and talking about the paintings; now I can’t bring myself to prepare, and I keep putting things off. I keep going over it in my mind, blaming security, my supervisor, even the school that booked the tour—anyone who “should have” prevented it. At the same time, I feel so ashamed, like I failed those children somehow.

I’ve become weirdly paralyzed by small decisions—what to wear, what to cook. My husband gets frustrated because I just stand there, stuck. And if someone drops something or comes up behind me, my heart pounds and my hands shake for a long time afterward; it takes ages to feel normal again. None of this has really eased up since it all happened.
D018-D020_h001.question_b:
It all really started after the flooding at the museum last spring—about two months after, I’d say. I wasn’t there when the pipe burst, but seeing the galleries ruined, some of the paintings warped, it just… hit me harder than I expected. Since then, I keep having these dreams maybe a few times a week. In them I’m back in the gallery and the water is creeping up the walls, and I wake up with that same heavy, sick feeling I had the first time I saw the damage.

I’ve become oddly stuck and unmotivated. I used to enjoy planning tours and tinkering with my scripts, but now even answering emails or prepping for a group feels like wading through mud. I catch myself replaying it all and getting angry at management—thinking, “If they’d fixed that leak when we first flagged it, this never would’ve happened.” At the same time, I feel almost ashamed, like I failed as a steward of the collection, even though I know logically it wasn’t my fault.

Day to day, I can’t make up my mind about simple things—what to wear, what to cook—so I just stand there stuck. And if someone startles me, my heart races and my hands shake for ages before I can settle down. This has all been going on continuously for a couple of months now. It started within a few weeks of the flood, and while it’s been distressing, I don’t feel like I’m “reliving” it constantly or avoiding the museum altogether—I still go in and do my tours, just… not like I used to.
